key_insight: The paper shows how to add trainable neural performance layers to plug-and-play distributed controllers while preserving closed-loop stability through built-in network gain bounds.
engineering_relevance: This lets networked systems adapt to topology changes and disturbances with better transient performance, without sacrificing the formal safety needed for modular deployment.
method: Uses an Internal Model Control (IMC) performance-boosting architecture that reduces stability to a finite ℓ2-gain condition.
Builds distributed neural operators that exchange information only with neighboring subsystems.
Derives free parametrizations that map unconstrained weights to gain-bounded interconnections, enabling unconstrained training without projection.
evidence_signal: A DC-microgrid case study in the abstract reports improved voltage transients under topology changes and load variations while maintaining nominal closed-loop stability.
watch_item: The network-norm parametrization may require network-wide information and can be more conservative or harder to update in fully decentralized settings.
paper_title: Distributed Performance Boosting through Neural Control for Plug-and-Play Networks
